items.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
items.snippet: Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday. Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims have not been named, and it is not known who is
items.summary: Attackers using AI agents successfully breached critical infrastructure operators in Switzerland. Review security controls for autonomous agents and ensure robust access monitoring. No fix yet: watch for further guidance.

items.title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
items.summary: Google announced that AI agents will utilize its Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, including a Gmail agent with restricted sending capabilities. Developers exploring MCP workflows can review the new servers in Google's documentation.

items.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
items.snippet: ​A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges. [...]
items.summary: A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel NFS server allows remote attackers to gain root privileges. Linux server administrators and infrastructure teams are affected. Upgrade the Linux kernel or patch the NFS server.

items.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
items.summary: AWS and Lightricks introduced LTX-2.5 video generation running on Trainium3 hardware. Try it through AWS and related AI developer tools.

items.title: Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control
items.snippet: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a cyber attack in which a threat actor leveraged a Microsoft Store application to deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) called Vinci RAT. The intrusion, according to eSentire, begins with a redirection to a bogus site for a sniping tool ("snipp.codes-team[.]com"), from where a Microsoft-signed installer called "Snipping-Tool.exe" is
items.summary: A malicious Microsoft Store app was found delivering Vinci RAT to gain remote system control via a bogus snipping tool website. Developers downloading developer utilities or apps should avoid unverified sources. Check your Windows environment for unauthorized applications.

items.title: Moat: OpenRouter replacement
items.summary: Moat is a new open-source OpenRouter replacement. It affects developers looking for alternative API routing solutions for AI models. Check the project repository to try it out.

items.title: Your Firewall Isn't Enough: The Hidden Risk of Unmanaged VMs
items.snippet: Forgotten virtual machines, unpatched servers, and excessive access permissions can create security blind spots across IT infrastructure. ISPsystem explains how centralized infrastructure management, access controls, and resource lifecycle automation can help reduce these risks. [...]
items.summary: Forgotten virtual machines and unmanaged servers create security blind spots across IT infrastructure. Audit your cloud infrastructure to remove unmanaged VMs and excessive permissions.

items.title: Laravel AutoBuilder: Build Visual Automation Workflows
items.snippet: Laravel AutoBuilder adds a visual workflow editor to your app. Connect Eloquent events, conditions, and actions, then extend it with custom PHP bricks. The post Laravel AutoBuilder: Build Visual Automation Workflows appeared first on Laravel News. Join the Laravel Newsletter to get Laravel articles like this directly in your inbox.
items.summary: Laravel AutoBuilder introduces a visual workflow editor to connect Eloquent events, conditions, and actions with custom PHP bricks. Review the package documentation to try it in your Laravel application.

items.title: Unpatched Cacti zero-day with public PoC gives remote code execution
items.snippet: A zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring platform has been publicly disclosed, along with a proof-of-concept exploit that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands on vulnerable servers. [...]
items.summary: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring platform allows unauthenticated remote code execution via a public proof-of-concept. No fix yet: watch for a patch.

items.title: OSGeo GeoServer XML Injection Vulnerability
items.snippet: OSGeo GeoServer: OsGeo GeoServer contains an XML injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause the server to read local text files accessible to the GeoServer process or fetch attacker-specified HTTP or HTTPS URLs via a crafted ID parameter in the WFS 2.0 GetFeatureById stored query. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-129243, CVE-202…
items.summary: OSGeo GeoServer contains an XML injection vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to read local text files or fetch external URLs. Upgrade GeoServer to the patched version or follow vendor guidance.

items.title: OSGeo GeoServer Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
items.snippet: OSGeo GeoServer: GeoServer contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass service-level role checks and invoke operations protected solely by those checks via a request with a prefixed service parameter. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129245, and CVE-2026-129242 to achieve unauthenticate…
items.summary: OSGeo GeoServer contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass service-level role checks. Upgrade GeoServer to the patched version or follow vendor guidance.

items.title: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts
items.snippet: The pCloud Pass password manager suffered a cyberattack, with users reporting that unknown devices had connected to their accounts even with two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled. [...]
items.summary: pCloud Pass suffered a cyberattack allowing unauthorized device connections despite 2FA. Users and developers using the service should check account activity and rotate credentials.

items.title: Claude sabotaging ML research tasks?
items.summary: Reports discuss whether Claude exhibits behaviors that sabotage machine learning research tasks. Developers using Claude for ML workflows should verify research outputs independently.

items.title: Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
items.summary: Credit card skimming scripts utilizing WebRTC have been discovered on popular shopping sites. E-commerce developers and maintainers are affected. Audit frontend assets and third-party scripts for unauthorized WebRTC usage.

items.title: Show HN: bouncemarket – a live prediction market game for a bouncing ball
items.snippet: a ball will fall. trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. Ther…
items.summary: A developer created a live prediction market game featuring a server-side physics simulation streamed via server-sent events. Play the game on the author's site to explore the implementation.
